articles.headline: Commanders' Jayden Daniels limited at practice, status up in air
articles.description: Jayden Daniels returned to practice in a limited capacity, but his status for games remains up in the air.
articles.body:
HERTFORDSHIRE, England -- Washington Commanders coach Dan Quinn said he needs to see more from quarterback Jayden Daniels before deciding whether he can play Sunday against the Colts. But it helps that they went through a similar situation last season.

Daniels dislocated his left elbow in a Week 2 loss at Dallas and returned to practice Wednesday. He was considered limited during what amounted to a 60-minute jog-through after the team arrived in Hertfordshire earlier in the morning.

"We won't put him out there before he's ready," Quinn said. "That's why it's important to trust the process. But him being back on the field, that's a good step for us."

Indeed it is. Daniels suffered the same injury in Week 9 last season and aggravated it upon his return five weeks later. Washington shut him down for the final four games of 2025.

But the team is optimistic that he'll return soon, whether against the Colts or potentially against the New York Giants a week later.

The Commanders (1-2) beat Seattle behind Marcus Mariota, who will start again Sunday if Daniels doesn't return.

On Wednesday, Daniels was wearing a black brace on his elbow that he'll keep on for the rest of the season. The brace leaves his arm slightly bent.

He took snaps from center during warmups, and he participated in footwork drills that ended with him throwing the ball, using his familiar motion. Daniels was smiling while wearing a baseball cap turned backward -- similar to his coach.

Quinn said Daniels would get more reps as the week progresses. Quinn said the timetable for his return will be centered on "the functionality and strength, the pain tolerance for him. He already has a high one."

The dislocated elbow in 2025 was Daniels' third injury that season; he also missed two games with a knee injury and another because of his hamstring. After his latest injury, Daniels visited multiple specialists in New York and Los Angeles who told him he could return without surgery, but surgery remains a possibility at some point.

Quinn has said they will rely on medical advice to help determine when Daniels is ready to play in a game.

"His drive is always strong to return to play," Quinn said. "Any athlete would probably tell you when you're going through something a second time there's a known entity of what the road looks like. We all feel that way. He does know what that process looks like and the mobility and the strength. There's a known entity of when you're ready."

Washington remains banged up. The Commanders already ruled out two starters: safety Nick Cross (internal injury) and guard Sam Cosmi (concussion). Neither traveled to England. Also, linebacker Frankie Luvu (groin) and tight end Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) will practice this week, but their status for Sunday remains uncertain.

articles.headline: Panthers CBs Jaycee Horn, Mike Jackson placed on IR
articles.description: The Panthers have placed starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn (quad) and Mike Jackson (groin) on injured reserve after both were injured in the Week 3 loss to the Browns.
articles.body:
The Carolina Panthers will be without their starting cornerback duo for at least the next four games as they placed Jaycee Horn (quad) and Mike Jackson (groin) on injured reserve Wednesday after both were injured in the Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns.

While Horn was expected to go on IR with what coach Dave Canales called a "significant" quad injury, Jackson's status had been open-ended. Jackson led the NFL with 19 pass breakups last season, and he and Horn combined for nine interceptions in 2025 as one of the most effective cornerback duos in the league.

Horn, who is coming off back-to-back Pro Bowl honors, was seeking a second opinion on his injury when NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Monday that he sustained a torn quad during the game-winning touchdown by the Browns. Jackson left Sunday's loss in the first half after falling awkward on a play that saw him get penalized in coverage.

The Panthers will need to rely on 2026 fourth-round pick Will Lee, Chau Smith-Wade and special teams ace Akayleb Evans with Horn and Jackson out of the mix. The team signed veteran Robert Rochell to the practice squad Wednesday. Corey Thornton, Zion Childress and undrafted rookie DeVonta Smith are also on the practice roster.

Canales, in addressing Horn's injury Monday, said replacing his top cornerback isn't possible, but now he will need to find replacements for both his starting boundary cover men.

"There's no replacing Jaycee Horn," Canales said. "He has had such an amazing offseason training camp, in season, just the energy, the preparation, all the different things. [He] has been amazing, has been really beautiful, so there's no replacing that. We're not asking our guys to replace Jaycee. We're just asking them to do their job."

Along with the ailments at cornerback, sources told NFL Network's Mike Garafolo and Rapoport on Tuesday that starting left guard Damien Lewis will be sidelined for a few weeks with an ulnar collateral ligament injury in an elbow. The Panthers are also monitoring injuries for starting quarterback Bryce Young (lower body), wide receivers Jalen Coker (quad) and Xavier Legette, safety Nick Scott (rib), and inside linebacker Devin Lloyd (calf).

With Coker and Legette questionable entering the week of work, the Panthers promoted veteran wide receiver David Moore from the practice squad. They also promoted running back Anthony Tyus III from the practice roster after he made his NFL debut against the Browns. Tyus will effectively slot into the third running back spot behind Chuba Hubbard and AJ Dillon with Jonathon Brooks on injured reserve.

Carolina hosts the Detroit Lions on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 4 before its bye week.

Following the bye, left tackle Ikem Ekwonu (PUP/patellar tendon), right tackle Taylor Moton (NFI/blood clot), defensive end Tershawn Wharton (PUP/neck), running back Trevor Etienne (IR/ankle), guard Brady Christensen (IR/hamstring) and linebacker Bam Martin-Scott (IR/hamstring) will be eligible to

articles.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Braelon Allen a worthy add, don't forget about Zach Charbonnet
articles.description: Those who ignored RBs in the draft are feeling the pain. Braelon Allen and Zach Charbonnet could help ease it.
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Sept. 30: Add Braelon Allen, stash Zach Charbonnet if you need RBs

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

How you doin', Vampire league managers?

Better yet, how about you zero-RB strategizers?

The 2026 season hasn't been the friendliest to those who went the cheap route at running back, at least not so far. Through three weeks, only two running backs selected outside the top 30 at the position on average have scored as many as 15 fantasy points in a game: Chuba Hubbard (twice) and Kyle Monangai. And anyone playing the Vampire format or going full zero-RB might not have even drafted either player, considering Hubbard went 34th and Monangai 37th; that'd be right around the four-running back average per team in the format.

A running back has scored at least 15 fantasy points on 35 occasions. Twenty-six, or 74%, came from top-15 positional picks. Fourteen, or 40%, came from the top eight. And six of the 11 games worth 25-plus points came from top-three backs Jahmyr Gibbs, Bijan Robinson and Jonathan Taylor.

That's not to dissuade zero-RB drafters, who have had success employing the strategy in the past and will probably fare better in the coming weeks as injuries and role changes take hold at the position. Besides, you've got the team you've got at this point, so you need to make the best of it.

Running back has been a particular focus of a couple of my teams this and last week, including in the Vampire league specifically, where the position's ho-hum stats have dug me a 0-3 hole. A pair of backfields who are not the altogether-too-obvious Miami Dolphins -- new leading man Ollie Gordon II was predictably the No. 1 free agent pickup overnight -- have my attention:

New York Jets: It's Braelon Allen, not Gordon, who was my primary focus on the pickups front, after news that usual starter Breece Hall's thigh injury late in Week 3 is a week-to-week, rather than day-to-day, injury. A big, powerful back, Allen might share rushing work with Isaiah Davis while Hall heals, but Allen is a capable fill-in starter with a good matchup in Week 4 (@CHI). I'm anticipating 12-15 carries and top odds on any goal-line carries, and that'd be a pretty good find off free agency for those seeking running back help (which should really be everyone).

Seattle Seahawks: Jadarian Price's fumbling problem is clearly an issue, as it's rare to see a first-round draft pick and Week 1 starter benched three games into his NFL career. articles.headline: Buccaneers put WR McMillan on IR, add QB Rypien to practice squad
articles.description: The Buccaneers placed wide receiver Jalen McMillan on injured reserve Wednesday, sidelining him for at least the next four games.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers placed wide receiver Jalen McMillan on injured reserve Wednesday, sidelining him for at least the next four games.

A source told ESPN's Jenna Laine earlier this week that McMillan suffered a PCL sprain in his left knee during Sunday's loss to the Minnesota Vikings, a reaggravation of an injury he suffered in training camp. The early thinking, per the source, was that McMillan could be sidelined for six to eight weeks.

The Buccaneers on Wednesday also signed veteran quarterback Brett Rypien to their practice squad, giving the team another veteran backup with starter Baker Mayfield set to miss at least the next three weeks because of a dislocated right thumb. The Buccaneers also have quarterback Easton Stick on their practice squad.

Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will take over as the starter beginning this week against the Green Bay Packers.

McMillan suffered his injury colliding with Vikings safety Josh Metellus while attempting to catch a pass on a corner route. He doesn't have a catch this season in two games. He missed the Buccaneers' opener with his previous knee injury, which forced him to miss multiple weeks during training camp.

The Buccaneers also signed safety Ifeatu Melifonwu to the 53-man roster from the practice squad Wednesday.

articles.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
articles.description: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
articles.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

articles.headline: Independent Football Regulator chief: Man City guilty verdict 'raises serious issues'
articles.description: Manchester City's guilty verdict for breaching Premier League financial rules "raises serious issues", according to the chair of English football's independent regulator.
articles.body:
Manchester City's guilty verdict for breaching Premier League financial rules "raises serious issues," according to the chair of English football's independent regulator.

An independent commission has concluded City "clearly intended to circumvent Premier League rules" by inflating revenue and hiding costs over a nine-season period.

David Kogan, the chair of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR), pointed out his body has the power to assess the suitability of club owners and executives "where appropriate," when there is "clear evidence of wrongdoing by individuals."

City have already indicated their intention to appeal, describing the decision as "unsafe," and drew support from former manager Pep Guardiola in an X post on Wednesday afternoon.

Kogan acknowledged the City case remains ongoing but outlined the powers the IFR could bring into play should the appeal board broadly uphold the decision of the original commission.

"The independent commission's decision raises serious issues," Kogan said.

"The IFR has powers to assess the suitability of owners, directors and executives and we will use these powers where appropriate, in the interests of protecting the sustainability, honesty and integrity of English football where there is clear evidence of wrongdoing by individuals.

"This includes taking account of findings made by the leagues. However, as the proceedings remain ongoing between Manchester City and the Premier League we will await further developments.

"We hope it can be resolved quickly for the sake of fans. For now, we have no further comment."

In the most extreme cases, the IFR has statutory powers to force directors and managers off boards and to compel owners to divest from clubs.

Guardiola, who won six Premier League titles with City before leaving at the end of last season, issued a social media post via the Pep Team X account in solidarity with the club's bosses, players, coach and supporters.

"I want every single Man City fan to know I am here; more than ever. I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran, the players, staff, Enzo and you, our unique supporters," the post read.

"Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all."

City were found to have engaged in schemes to inflate revenue and hide costs to the tune of more than £900 million ($1.2b billion) to avoid breaching Premier League and UEFA rules.

The club have already indicated their intention to appeal, and have said the decision "contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe."

City chief executive Ferran Soriano told staff in a video message that the commission had gone along with the Premier League's "conspiracy theory."

articles.headline: Does Man City's guilty verdict impact Pep Guardiola's legacy as an all-time coaching great?
articles.description: Pep Guardiola won 16 major honors as Man City manager. They all now count for nothing after the Premier League found the club guilty of systematically breaking financial rules.
articles.headlineJa: マンCの有罪判決は、史上最高の名将ペップ・グアルディオラのレガシーに影響を与えるのか？
articles.descriptionJa: ペップ・グアルディオラ監督はマンCで16の主要タイトルを獲得した。しかし、プレミアリーグが同クラブによる組織的な財務ルール違反を認定したため、それらはすべて無意味なものとなってしまった。
articles.body:
Pep Guardiola won 16 major honors during his 10-year reign as Manchester City manager before he left in the summer. They all now count for nothing.

Under Guardiola, City won a Champions League-Premier League-FA Cup treble. They became the only club in English history to win four successive league titles. They were the first team to achieve a domestic treble, and the only side to win the title by amassing 100 points. All of it was built on a false premise.

To borrow a phrase from the Premier League statement that condemned the club's "systematic rule-breaking for almost a decade" following an independent commission's finding that City were guilty of more than 100 breaches of rules between 2009-2018, it was all a "sham."

Man City? Sham City more like.

- Marcotti: Hard to see how City recover from extraordinary guilty verdict

- Dawson: Man City's guilt the talk of the town around English soccer

- Watch: Full reaction to 'the biggest sporting cheating scandal ever'

The egregious actions of City's owners -- Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al Nahyan's Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) -- and executives has destroyed the reputation of a 146-year-old club. City have said they will appeal the verdict, and they maintain they are innocent, but Guardiola cannot escape the damage caused by a prolonged and systematic program of financial deception because much of it was done for his benefit.

Abu Dhabi built a club and a team fit for Guardiola, but it was a construction built by ill-gotten gains. The advantages Guardiola had at his disposal are now proved to have been unfair. As former Manchester United captain Roy Keane said this week: "[City] won it on the pitch because cheating was going on."

Financial mismanagement, chicanery, deception -- whatever you want to call it, the foundations of Guardiola's City empire are rooted in the rule-breaking that happened before and during his time as manager, so his record-breaking era at the club is tainted by all of it.

But there are two sides to the Guardiola story at City. The former Barcelona and Bayern Munich coach arrived at the Etihad in the summer of 2016 having already won six league titles in Catalonia and Bavaria, as well as two Champions Leagues with Barça. His status as the world's preeminent coach was already secure.

Guardiola is a coaching genius, a man whose tactical brilliance built arguably the world's greatest-ever club side at Barcelona. He reinvented the way the game was played, and his influence is now seen at every level of the game.

It's why City's Abu Dhabi hierarchy, led by Sheikh Mansour and club chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak -- who is also CEO of Mubadala, Abu Dhabi's sovereign wealth fund, and holds senior positions within the Abu Dhabi government -- made such strenuous efforts to hire Guardiola in the first place.

articles.headlineJa: NBAが新ガイドラインを発表、審判にプッシュオフの厳格な取り締まりを指示
articles.descriptionJa: NBAは審判に対し、プッシュオフを含む「発生頻度が高く、影響の大きい」4種類のファウル判定に関する新たな指導を行いました。

articles.headline: Kessler talks up Lakers' title hopes behind 'nasty' defense
articles.description: New addition Walker Kessler is convinced the Lakers have the right guys to be "a nasty defensive team" and a contender in the Western Conference this season.
articles.headlineJa: ケスラー、「エグい」守備を武器にレイカーズの優勝への期待を語る
articles.descriptionJa: 新加入のウォーカー・ケスラーは、今季のレイカーズには「強力でエグい守備チーム」となり、ウェスタン・カンファレンスの優勝争いに加わるための適切なメンバーが揃っていると確信しています。

articles.headline: Sources: NBA reviewing bids from three finalists for Vegas team
articles.description: The NBA is expected to select the winning bid for owner of the Las Vegas expansion team from among three finalist groups: Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; and Bill Foley and Jerry Colangelo.
articles.headlineJa: 情報筋：NBA、ベガス新球団創設に向けて最終候補3組の買収提案を審査中
articles.descriptionJa: NBAは、ラスベガスの拡充チームのオーナー決定に向け、ナンシー・ウォルトン・ローリー＆ビル・ローリー組、スティーブ・アポストロポロス＆マーク・ラスリー組、ビル・フォーリー＆ジェリー・コランジェロ組の最終候補3グループの中から落札者を選定する見込みです。

articles.headline: NBA preseason buzz: Latest on trades, news and intel
articles.description: The NBA regular season is less than a month away, and we're tracking all the news, deals, and trades across the league.
articles.headlineJa: NBAプレシーズンの話題：トレード、ニュース、最新情報まとめ
articles.descriptionJa: NBAレギュラーシーズン開幕まで1か月を切り、リーグ全体の最新ニュース、契約、トレード情報をまとめてお伝えします。
